entry.name: UVTA
entry.title: Unified Visual-Tactile-Action Modeling from Human Demonstrations for Dexterous Manipulation
entry.summary: Right-hand demonstrations of 5 contact-rich tasks from people wearing a passive 22-DoF exoskeleton glove with fingertip FSR arrays (5,000) and from a teleoperated Sharpa Wave hand on a Sharpa North robot (749), released as 20 fingertip-region touch values, wrist fisheye video and 22 joint angles at 30 Hz.
entry.hand: Human right hand in a passive 22-DoF exoskeleton glove (fingertip FSR arrays); Sharpa Wave (22 DoF), right hand of a fixed-base Sharpa North

sensor.note: Released field tactile (T, 20) float32 for both embodiments: 5 fingertips (thumb, index, middle, ring, little) x 4 regions (A tip = 5 taxels, B side = 3, C middle = 9, D side = 3), each the mean of its taxels. Human: FSR array of 20 taxels per fingertip read from a 240-value glove payload (blocks 0-19, 40-59, 80-99, 120-139, 160-179), raw counts (region means up to ~1,700 in the checked episodes). Robot: Sharpa Wave fingertip deformation maps (240x240 grayscale) summed per glove-taxel region by a fixed pixel-to-taxel map, then averaged per region (VTPM); values up to ~140,000 in the checked episodes. Raw taxels, Sharpa tactile images, deformation maps and the fingertip force magnitudes named in the metadata are not released. The paper subtracts a per-recording baseline (human: mean of first 5 frames; robot: first frame).
sensor.maker: not stated (FSR exoskeleton glove); robot: Sharpa
sensor.model: FSR fingertip arrays on a passive 22-DoF exoskeleton glove; robot: Sharpa Wave fingertip tactile sensor

scale.text: 5,749 episodes over 5 tasks: 5,000 human (1,000 per task) + 749 robot (150 per task, 149 for flip_book); ~19.7 h at 30 Hz (16.3 h human, 3.4 h robot; derived from file counts); 482 GB

entry.access: Hugging Face Chopper233/UVTA, ungated, 28 tar shards (5-22 GB each, 482 GB in total) of Zarr v2 episode stores, one set of shards per task and embodiment.
caveats: Touch is released only as 20 pooled values per frame (4 regions per fingertip); raw glove taxels, Sharpa tactile images, deformation maps and fingertip forces are not in the release.

Robot touch is derived from Sharpa Wave deformation maps by a fixed pixel-to-glove-taxel map (VTPM), so robot values (up to ~140,000) and human FSR counts (up to ~1,700 in the checked episodes) are on different scales; neither is in physical units.
Right hand only: the robot has two Sharpa Wave hands, but only the right arm, right hand and right wrist camera are released. Fingertips only, no phalanx or palm sensing.
Robot demonstrations use one fixed scene per task (layout, start pose, table height); human demonstrations vary objects, backgrounds and glove colour (black or white).
Human actions are derived: hand_action and pose_action are the next frame's joint angles and wrist pose.
No per-frame timestamps and no object, scene or operator labels; 30 Hz is the paper's resampling rate. The robot metadata names a head stereo camera that is not released.
Per-frame RGB is stored as blosc-lz4 Zarr chunks inside large tar shards with no per-episode byte offsets; fetching one episode means walking the tar headers or streaming the shard from its start.
Many episodes are shorter than 10 s (mean 7.7 s for robot switch, 8.7 s for human flip_book, 9.1 s for human switch).

tracking.system: passive 22-DoF linkage exoskeleton (carbon-fibre links, dorsal mount, joint encoders)
tracking.note: human; encoder FK -> fingertip poses in the Sharpa Wave palm frame -> constrained IK to the 22 Sharpa Wave joint angles, released as proprioception

tracking.system: HTC VIVE Tracker 3.0 x 2 (one fixed to the table as reference, one on the wrist via a 3D-printed adapter)
tracking.note: human; released as pose (xyz + rotation vector) in the robot base frame after calibration

tracking.system: Sharpa Wave right-hand joint angles (22) and commanded targets
Sharpa North right-arm forward kinematics (arm joints + 5 torso motors)
tracking.note: robot; observed and commanded end-effector pose
robot demonstrations are teleoperated; the teleoperation device is not stated

other: commanded wrist pose and 22 hand joint targets (robot: teleop commands; human: next-frame state)

unconfirmed: frames = 2,124,537 and hours = 19.7 derived from MANIFEST.json: per shard, frames = n_files - 14 x n_episodes - 1, since each episode holds T per-frame RGB chunk files plus 14 metadata and array files and each shard one task-level .zgroup (checked on the two extracted episodes: 280 = 266 + 14, 321 = 307 + 14). 2,124,537 / 30 Hz = 19.7 h; human 1,758,592 frames (16.3 h), robot 365,945 (3.4 h). Mean episode length by task (human / robot): flip_book 8.7 / 9.7 s, light_bulb 13.6 / 31.3 s, switch 9.1 / 7.7 s, ball 10.2 / 12.6 s, tube 17.1 / 20.1 s.

taxels_per_hand = 100 from the release metadata (fsr_layout: 20 taxels per finger at glove payload blocks 0-19 ... 160-179) and deform_to_human/fsr_region.py; the paper describes each fingertip FSR array as 'four sensing regions, each with an active area of 15 x 15 mm2', which matches the 4 pooled regions. The glove payload has 240 values; whether the other 140 positions carry sensors is not stated (the paper says sensing is fingertip-only).
Glove maker, FSR model, native glove sampling rate and force range are not stated; a code comment in deform_to_human/core.py refers to a '~0..4095 glove scale' (12-bit ADC, inferred).
Robot platform name 'Sharpa North' (fixed base, two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands) is from the paper; the release metadata names URDF north_poc2_2 and station POC22002 in the source paths.
Pose xyz unit not stated (values 0.15-1.1, consistent with metres); joint-angle unit not stated (range about -0.4 to 1.25, consistent with radians).
Wrist camera model and native resolution not stated; released frames are 480x384 RGB (resize_hw [384, 480]). The decoded robot and human frames are fisheye views with near-neutral colour.
Collection dates from source file paths in the episode metadata: human 2026-07-05 to 2026-08-21, robot 2026-07-08 to 2026-08-22 (shard-first and probed episodes only).
Human B_side regions were zero for the whole switch human episode_0 but active in flip_book human episode_3; no dead region is claimed.
subjects not stated: human source folders carry names such as ZZH-0705, tablecloth-170, light-100, ball_1_ego, dropper_ego, which are not documented.

Overlap with SharpaDex v1.0: its 495 seasons span 2026-03 to 2026-07-07 on stations POC22002/07/18/21/27/32/48/50/54/61/65 (POC22002 only in deal_playing_cards, 2026-07-01 to 07-03); the UVTA robot seasons seen (POC22002, 2026-07-08 to 08-22) are not among them, and SharpaDex is bimanual LeRobot with 60-D fingertip wrench and tactile videos. Related task themes exist (SharpaDex turn_book_pages, transfer_liquid_with_dropper). Checked by season names of 6 robot shard-first episodes and 20 probed robot episodes, not every UVTA episode.

Overlap with T-Rex (catalog trex): different platform (Dexmate Vega-1 + two Sharpa Wave, robot_type dexmate_vega1_and_sharpa_wave), format (LeRobot v3) and tasks. UVTA uses the pretrained T-Rex model as a baseline post-trained on UVTA robot demos; the paper does not train on the T-Rex dataset or any other public dataset.

download.format: 28 uncompressed tar shards <task>/<embodiment>-NNNNN.tar, each holding Zarr v2 stores <task>/<embodiment>/episode_<k>/ with camera_0/rgb (one blosc-lz4 chunk per frame), tactile, proprioception, hand_action, pose, pose_action (one blosc-lz4 chunk each) and .zattrs meta_json; MANIFEST.json lists episode ids, file counts and SHA-256 per shard
download.total_size: 482 GB (482,351,124,480 B of tar; human 408.7 GB, robot 69.7 GB)
download.per_episode: ~35-200 MB (RGB dominates: ~150-260 kB per frame); non-RGB arrays < 100 kB
download.partial_fetch: HTTP range requests on the shard: hop tar headers (each episode starts with its .zattrs, the RGB chunks are in lexicographic order, tactile/0.0 is the last member) to read T and the touch array with ~5 requests (~1.6 MB) per episode; one whole episode is one contiguous byte range

channels.name: camera_0/rgb
channels.frame: right-wrist fisheye camera (robot: observe/vision/right_wrist/fisheye/rgb; human: camera on the exoskeleton calibrated to the robot's camera-to-end-effector transform)
channels.note: both embodiments; one blosc-lz4 Zarr chunk per frame; camera model not stated

channels.name: tactile (human)
channels.unit: raw glove counts, region mean (not stated; up to ~1,700 seen)
channels.frame: [thumb, index, middle, ring, little] x [A tip (5 taxels), B side (3), C middle (9), D side (3)]; right hand, B = thumb side, D = little side
channels.note: FSR glove source tactile/glove/right/values (240-value payload, fingertip blocks of 20) pooled by fsr_region.py; nearest-time aligned to camera frames

channels.name: tactile (robot)
channels.unit: sum of grayscale deformation-map pixels per glove-taxel region, region mean (up to ~140,000 seen; 0 at rest)
channels.frame: same 20-column layout as the human glove
channels.note: derived from Sharpa Wave observe/tactile/right_<finger>/deform (240x240 grayscale) by the region maps in deform_to_human/glove_sharpa_mapping; the deform maps and the per-finger force magnitudes listed in .zattrs are not released

channels.name: proprioception (human)
channels.note: exoskeleton encoders -> fingertip FK -> constrained IK to Sharpa Wave joints (state/retarget/right_hand/joint/position)

channels.name: hand_action
channels.note: robot: raw teleop command stream action/right_hand/joint_angle; human: proprioception shifted by +1 frame (last frame repeated)

channels.name: pose
channels.unit: xyz not stated (metres by range) + axis-angle rotation vector (rad)
channels.note: robot: FK of right-arm joints + torso motors[:5] from the north_poc2_2 URDF; human: VIVE wrist tracker relative to the table tracker, retargeted (state/retarget/right_hand_pose)

channels.name: pose_action
channels.note: robot: FK of commanded arm joints; human: pose shifted by +1 frame

channels.name: .zattrs meta_json
channels.note: source HDF5 path (task, station or session folder, date), T, valid window into the source, channel sources and layouts

episode_index.where: MANIFEST.json (per shard: task, embodiment, episode ids, n_files, tar_bytes, sha256) + per-episode .zattrs meta_json (T, source file path)
episode_index.note: episode ids restart at episode_0 per task and embodiment. No object, scene, operator or success labels. Paper task names: flip_book = Flip Page, light_bulb = Screw Light Bulb, switch = Toggle Switch, ball = Ball Classification, tube = Liquid Transfer with a Dropper.

sample.reason: Public, ungated HF release under Apache-2.0 (dataset card metadata), which allows redistribution with attribution. Both embodiments carry touch, so each task gets one human and one robot episode. Label the collection 'Apache-2.0'.

327 frames. All 20 columns non-zero; 13 regions in contact for >= 1 s on thumb, middle, ring and little (thumb A 4.8 s, peak 686; little D peak 561). Of human episodes 0-7, only 3, 4 and 6 reach 10 s.

sample.fetch_estimate: ~960 MB: the 10 episodes are contiguous byte ranges in their shards (listed per episode, 46-197 MB each, RGB dominates); switch/human/episode_0 is already extracted (/tmp/claude-1003/-home-yxma-src-visual-wrist-tactile-cosmos/d1a1d10f-d10b-45ec-a896-918e856e78ff/scratchpad/survey_uvta/dl_human). Re-hosted media: one 480x384 fisheye stream per episode re-encoded to H.264 (few MB each). Episode JSON: 20 touch + 22 joint values per frame at 30 Hz, < 1 MB.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 5 tasks (<= 6), all taken. Episodes: one per task per embodiment, 10 in total (the upper limit), because both the glove and the robot carry touch and they are recorded with different sensors. Candidates: the first episodes of each shard, read with tar-header range reads (37 episodes probed: T from .zattrs, tactile array decoded). Contact: a region above its baseline (human mean of first 5 frames, robot first frame, as in the paper) by max(10% of the episode range, 50 counts human / 2,000 robot) for >= 1 s. Length: all picks 10.2-27.6 s, no window cut. All 20 tactile columns are present in every pick; columns that stay 0 are named in 'why'. Budget within 2 MB JSON, ~30 MB media per episode and 20 GB download.
deviations: Two episodes per task (one per embodiment) instead of one per task; total stays at 10.
Episodes were picked from the start of each shard (cheapest to reach); no random sampling across the full release.
